title: Collection expressions ([...] syntax)
hook: C# 12 introduced bracket syntax — [1, 2, 3] — to replace the noisy new List<int> { 1, 2, 3 } pattern. The brackets always create a real collection in memory; they are not a lazy query.

blocks.text: A collection expression is a bracketed list of elements: [1, 2, 3] or ["read", "write"]. The compiler converts it to an array, List<T>, Span<T>, ImmutableArray<T>, or any type with a suitable collection builder. The spread operator .. inlines elements from another collection: [..first, ..second]. The empty form [] can become Array.Empty<T>() when the target will not be mutated. Collection expressions arrived in C# 12 and are the modern way to write literal collections.

entries.plainDefinition: Bracket syntax [e1, e2, ...] that the compiler converts into a concrete collection type based on context.
entries.example: List<int> nums = [1, 2, 3]; creates a List with three items.

entries.plainDefinition: The .. prefix before an enumerable inlines all its elements into the new collection.
entries.example: [..listA, ..listB] copies every element from both lists into one new list.

entries.plainDefinition: All elements are read and stored immediately — not deferred until someone loops.
entries.example: IEnumerable<int> x = [..hugeList]; still allocates a full in-memory collection.

entries.plainDefinition: A read-only array wrapper from System.Collections.Immutable that cannot be changed after creation.

blocks.text: Collection expressions cut boilerplate for the most common collection creation pattern. A tiny allow-list of auth scopes, a batch of message IDs, or a set of poison-queue keys all read cleaner with brackets. But they always materialize — converting to IEnumerable<T> still allocates every element. Do not replace a streaming CSV yield with [..allRows]. For literals and small spreads, they are the right default in modern C#.

blocks.title: Always eager, never lazy
blocks.body: Collection expressions are not LINQ. [..query] copies every element into a new collection right away. Use yield or LINQ Select for deferred sequences.

items.title: Write the bracket syntax
items.body: [1, 2, 3] or ["a", "b"] — elements separated by commas inside square brackets.

items.title: Compiler picks the target type
items.body: The left-hand side or parameter type decides: int[], List<int>, Span<int>, ImmutableArray<int>, etc.

items.title: Spread inlines elements
items.body: ..existingCollection copies every element from the source into the new collection.

items.title: Result is materialized
items.body: Every element is stored in memory immediately. No deferred execution.

diagram.title: Collection expression targets
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  CE["[1, 2, ..rest]"] --> T{Target type?}
  T -->|int[]| A[Heap array]
  T -->|List int| L[Growable list]
  T -->|Span int| S[Stack slice]
  T -->|ImmutableArray| I[Frozen array]
  T -->|IEnumerable int| E[Still allocates in memory]

snippet.label: Batch IDs and spread
snippet.explanation: Spreads copy elements into a new list. The first line materializes all message IDs. The third line merges both collections into one.

snippet.label: HashSet with comparer
snippet.explanation: Collection expressions work with HashSet, arrays, and other collection types. For comparers, you may still need the constructor — check overload resolution.

snippet.label: Empty collection and Span target
snippet.explanation: Empty [] can optimize to Array.Empty. Span targets follow ref-struct rules (module 17). Collection expressions cannot be default parameter values or constants.

blocks.title: Spread syntax comparison
rows: Not allowed as const or default param

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Thinking [..query] is as lazy as query — it copies every element immediately. Using collection expressions as default parameter values — that is a compile error. Ambiguous overloads when both List and Span are applicable without an explicit cast.

interviewTakeaways: Introduced in C# 12; [e1, e2, ..rest] is the syntax.
Always eager; IEnumerable<T> target still allocates.
Can target arrays, List, Span, immutable collections, and builder-attributed types.
commonPitfalls: Thinking [..query] is as lazy as query.
Using collection expressions as default parameter values (illegal).
Ambiguous overloads when both List and Span are applicable without a cast.

jsTsCorrelations.note: [...a, ...b] in JS always makes a new Array. C# [..a, ..b] makes whatever the target type is.
TS as const freezes literal types. C# collection expressions pick a BCL collection type from context, not a tuple type unless you target a tuple.
